source.scope: Proposal-only procedures for EXT-F-4121-T01 through EXT-F-4124-T01. No canonical inventory/status changes and no runtime execution.
source.manual_execution_route: In a signed-in member or admin profile: side panel > Tools > Catalog, choose Internal or All surface if needed, search the exact tool, expand, replace JSON and Run. ToolsView validates local argsSchema, then calls handler.run directly with conversationId=null, runId=manual-test, permissionMode=act, assignedTabId=null and emits local TOOL_TIMELINE_EVENT started/completed/error. This bypasses dispatch.ts permission/approval routing and aidream execution. TOOL_ASK_USER_REQUEST is still broadcast to the inbox; its null conversation falls back to the currently selected chat, where the card can be answered. A manual result is UI handler evidence only; it does not create the server tool call/message lifecycle or prove streamed tool_event/tool message persistence.
source.build_reload_identity: Before any eventual execution, follow docs/stabilization/PLAN.md § Build and reload contract: resource permit and receipt with source/dirty hash, lockfile/output hashes, WXT mode, extension runtime ID, Chrome version, actual profile/auth/role/org, permissions, backend, fixture IDs and timestamp. Verify the loaded unpacked runtime/build. After relevant build/config changes reload extension, reopen side panel and confirm replacement identity. DevTools-open inspection is not evidence of idle worker restart.
source.role_applicability: Run member and admin separately and retain separate observations. The inventory marks guest not applicable because Tools requires sign-in; guest denial belongs to the Tools UI case. Role applicability does not imply an admin-only restriction: current metadata marks these bindings admin_only=false. Do not change the existing guest/member/admin status cells from this proposal.

EXT-F-4121-T01.title: Controlled manual execution: user
preconditions_fixtures: Complete shared build/reload identity and role setup above. Select an existing disposable test conversation in the side panel before opening Tools so null-conversation ask cards can fall back to that selected conversation.

Use only non-sensitive synthetic content. Do not use type=secret, enter secrets, or send a real notification. The handler's prompt/response can expose input in UI receipts. No backend fixture is needed for a simple question.
steps: In the selected test conversation, run {"type":"choice","question":"Procedure fixture: choose the marked option","options":["fixture-A","fixture-B"],"context":"owned manual tool procedure","timeout_seconds":60}.
Confirm the ask card appears in the side-panel inbox for the selected conversation; choose fixture-B and submit. Observe the inline manual runner output and that the card disappears.

Run {"type":"choice","question":"Procedure fixture: cancellation control","options":["fixture-A","fixture-B"],"timeout_seconds":60} and cancel the card. Record the explicit cancelled result. Do not leave it waiting for timeout.

Run {"type":"choice","question":"invalid input control","options":[],"timeout_seconds":60}. Confirm local schema/refinement validation reports the invalid choice before handler execution and no ask card appears.
After a full extension reload and reopening Tools, repeat the positive choice once. Record this as a separate warm-after-reload observation, not worker-idle restart evidence.
expected: Positive: the card visibly contains the synthetic question/options and returns an answer envelope with selected=["fixture-B"], cancelled=false, timed_out=false; the Tools runner shows the direct handler output. Cancellation returns cancelled=true and removes the card.

The invalid options input is rejected by local schema validation and emits no card. Notification permission is not exercised by this choice case; the catalog declares notifications for user generally, but this chosen branch does not call fireSystemNotification.

Only direct manual handler/card behavior is evidenced. The manual timeline event is local UI state, not an aidream tool_event or persisted role=tool message. Dispatcher gating, live agent invocation, streaming delivery, message persistence, permission denial and cold worker restart remain unverified.
EXT-F-4121-T01.cleanup: Resolve or cancel every synthetic pending card before leaving the conversation. No persistent backend data is created by this chosen branch.

EXT-F-4122-T01.title: Controlled manual execution: request_user_takeover
preconditions_fixtures: Complete shared build/reload identity and role setup above. Select an existing disposable test conversation so the inbox can associate the null-conversation manual request with the selected chat.

Omit tab_id: this avoids focusing another tab and isolates the takeover request/card behavior. Use synthetic reason/instructions only; do not claim browser control was transferred based on the card alone.
steps: Run {"reason":"Owned manual takeover procedure","instructions":"Read the visible fixture page and report its heading in this card","expected_action":"Reply with the word fixture-complete","timeout_seconds":60}.

Confirm the inbox card displays the reason and both instructions and expected action, separated into readable text. Reply with the synthetic text fixture-complete, then inspect the runner output and card removal.
Run {"reason":"invalid control","timeout_seconds":0}. Confirm local schema validation rejects the value before handler execution and no card appears.
Reload the extension, reopen Tools, select the same test conversation and repeat the positive request once; record it separately.
expected: The valid call produces an ask card whose question includes reason, instructions and expected_action; the user reply resolves with answer fixture-complete, cancellation false and any additional note null unless entered. This proves a user-facing takeover request/response prompt only.
The invalid timeout is rejected by the runner's schema validation. No tab activation occurs because tab_id is omitted.

Direct manual execution does not establish agent pause/resume, tab assignment, server tool_event, persisted tool message, dispatcher permission gate or live binding behavior. Those require a real agent-dispatched conversation fixture; none is supplied here, so keep those acceptance dimensions unverified.
EXT-F-4122-T01.cleanup: Resolve the ask card by replying before leaving. No browser tab state or backend data is changed by the proposed inputs.

EXT-F-4123-T01.title: Controlled manual execution: update_plan
preconditions_fixtures: Complete shared build/reload identity and role setup above. Select an existing disposable test conversation and open its plan/tasks panel before running.

Use synthetic plan content and omit domains to avoid implying that browser navigation is authorized. Direct Tools execution passes conversationId=null: it can render and answer the approval card but deliberately skips savePlan/setPlanStatus/addTasks persistence. Therefore this procedure is only a manual prompt/result smoke; persistence/approval-to-task acceptance requires a real agent-dispatched conversation fixture and must remain unverified without one.
steps: Run {"title":"Owned plan procedure","steps":["Inspect the owned test conversation","Record the visible result"],"reasoning":"Synthetic manual procedure","estimated_minutes":2,"timeout_seconds":60}.
Confirm the approval card displays title, reasoning, ordered steps and estimate. Select Reject to avoid creating follow-on tasks; inspect the direct handler result and card removal.
Confirm the selected conversation's plan panel has no newly persisted proposed/rejected plan from this manual call. Treat this as expected direct-run limitation, not as successful persistence.
Run {"steps":[],"timeout_seconds":60}. Confirm local validation rejects the empty steps array and no card appears.
Reload extension and reopen the same Tools route; repeat the valid synthetic prompt and reject it. Do not infer persistence across reload from this route.
expected: The card shows the synthetic plan fields and Reject returns approved=false with a rejection note/result. The empty steps input is rejected before handler execution.

No plan persistence or task population is expected when invoked manually because conversationId is null; absence from the panel is not evidence that the agent path works. A passing card interaction cannot close the inventory's broader plan behavior.

Live agent invocation, plan proposal storage, accepted/rejected status persistence, auto-population into chat.agent_task, tool_event/tool message persistence, dispatcher gates and cold worker restart remain unverified without a real agent-dispatched conversation fixture.
EXT-F-4123-T01.cleanup: Reject the proposal and clear any ask card. Since conversationId is null, the proposed path should not create local plan or task records.

EXT-F-4124-T01.title: Controlled manual execution: user_todos
not_executable_reasons: Every user_todos branch requires ctx.conversationId. ToolsView invokes the handler with conversationId=null, so its actual result is {ok:false,reason:'No active conversation'} before list/add/update/remove/mark_done/clear_done branches. The manual runner cannot exercise the seven inventory controls or establish their persistence.

The required real agent-dispatched conversation fixture is absent from this assignment. Do not fabricate a conversation ID in the manual UI or claim that a handler result from another route proves agent dispatch. A future procedure must obtain a genuine owned test conversation through normal UI and invoke user_todos from the real agent path, with its real conversation ID supplied by dispatch.
future_fixture_requirements: Use a disposable real conversation in both member and admin profiles, created through normal UI and bound to the genuine selected conversation. Do not inject a session, mock services, edit extension storage, or send a fabricated conversation ID.

Use unique synthetic title/context strings. Execute add with silent=true to avoid notification side effects; capture returned owned todo id. Then list, update title/context, mark_done true and false, remove, and clear_done using only that owned fixture todo. To exercise clear_done positively, add a second owned item and mark only it done before clearing. Verify state in the conversation's TaskPanel and after extension reload; confirm unrelated baseline todos remain unchanged.
Include schema-negative input and unknown owned ID controls, and capture the actual agent tool event/result plus rendered tool message; preserve raw message content only if sanitized synthetic text.

limitations: Source and rendered-component review only; none of these proposals was run in Chrome. No runtime pass/fail or role status is asserted.

Manual Tools execution is direct handler invocation with conversationId=null and permissionMode=act. It cannot stand in for the registered live agent dispatcher, server streaming, persisted role=tool message or normal Ask/Act permission gate.

No real agent-dispatched owned conversation fixture was provided. user_todos is explicitly NOT_EXECUTABLE on the manual route; update_plan persistence and agent tool-message outcomes remain unverified even if its manual ask card is observed.
Member/admin roles remain separate applicable modes; guest remains N/A per current inventory because Tools requires sign-in. This patch does not modify canonical inventory or status cells.
